Simulation-based infit MSQ cutoffs

Source: R/infit_cutoff.R
RMitemInfitCutoff.Rd

Simulates datasets from a Rasch or partial credit model that fits and resembles your data, and computes the conditional infit and outfit MSQ of every item in each. Passed to RMitemInfit(), the result gives bootstrap p-values corrected across items, and an interval per item that describes where a fitting item's statistic is expected to fall.

Usage

RMitemInfitCutoff(
  data,
  iterations = 400,
  parallel = TRUE,
  n_cores = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE,
  seed = NULL,
  cutoff_method = "hdci",
  hdci_width = 0.95,
  dgp = c("resample", "conditional")
)

Arguments

data

A data.frame or matrix of item responses, items scored from 0. Only complete cases (rows without NA) are used.

iterations

Integer. Number of simulated datasets. Default 400, the recommended minimum for reproducible decisions. Use 1000 to 2000 for a final analysis (Johansson, 2026).

parallel

Logical. Run the simulations in parallel via mirai when it is installed. Default TRUE.

n_cores

Integer or NULL. Number of parallel workers. When NULL, getOption("mc.cores") is used. If that is unset too, a warning is given and the simulations run sequentially.

verbose

Logical. Show a progress bar. Default FALSE.

seed

Integer or NULL. Random seed for reproducibility. See easyRasch2-reproducibility for what this guarantees and how it interacts with parallel.

cutoff_method

Character. How the interval per item is computed: "hdci" (default), the highest-density continuous interval from ggdist::hdci() (needs ggdist), or "quantile", the 2.5th to 97.5th percentiles.

hdci_width

Numeric. Width of the interval with cutoff_method = "hdci". Default 0.95. Ignored with "quantile".

The interval describes where a fitting item's statistic is expected to fall. It is not a decision rule. Flagging every item outside a width-w interval tests all k items at once, with a family-wise error rate of 1 - w^k, 37% for a 95% interval over nine items. Decisions come from the corrected p-value in RMitemInfit(). Up to version 1.1.1 the default was 0.999, which needs roughly 5000 iterations before the interval reaches its stated width. A 95% interval reaches it by about 1000 (Johansson, 2026).

dgp

Character. How datasets are simulated. "resample" (default) draws person locations from the WLE estimates with replacement and simulates responses from the model (a marginal null). "conditional" simulates each respondent's response pattern from the model given their observed total score, with the item parameters fixed (a conditional null). The conditional infit is itself conditional on the total score, so "conditional" is its natural null. Experimental.

Value

A list with:

results

data.frame with the columns iteration, Item, InfitMSQ and OutfitMSQ, one row per item and simulated dataset.

item_cutoffs

data.frame with the interval per item: Item, infit_low, infit_high, outfit_low, outfit_high, computed by cutoff_method.

actual_iterations

Number of simulated datasets that could be used. Everything downstream rests on this rather than on iterations, so it is the number to report.

requested_iterations

The iterations argument, so that callers can tell how many simulated datasets were left out.

sample_n

Number of complete cases used.

sample_n_total

Number of respondents in data, before the complete-case filter.

sample_has_na

Logical. Whether data contained missing values.

sample_summary

Summary of the WLE person locations.

item_names

Item names from data.

cutoff_method

"hdci" or "quantile".

hdci_width

The HDCI width (used only with "hdci").

dgp

"resample" or "conditional".

Details

The generating model has the CML item parameters (psychotools) and the WLE person locations of data. In each iteration a dataset is simulated by dgp, the model is refitted by CML (psychotools::pcmodel()), and the conditional infit and outfit MSQ are computed with iarm::out_infit(). A simulated dataset that cannot be refitted, for example because a response category is empty, is left out. RMitemInfit() reports how many were left out in its caption. A category used only by respondents with a zero or perfect total score stops the function before it simulates, since CML cannot estimate its threshold.

The method and the default settings come from simulation studies of detection (Johansson, 2025) and of iterations and multiplicity correction (Johansson, 2026).

Parallel processing needs the optional mirai package. The iarm package must be installed (it is in Suggests).

References

Johansson, M. (2025). Detecting item misfit in Rasch models. Educational Methods & Psychometrics, 3(18). doi:10.61186/emp.2025.5

Johansson, M. (2026). Simulation-based cutoffs for conditional item fit in Rasch models: Iterations, multiplicity correction, and decision stability. PsyArXiv. doi:10.31234/osf.io/7pqz4_v2

See also

RMitemInfit() for the test, RMitemInfitPlot() to plot the simulated values, RMitemInfitCutoffMI() for multiply imputed data.

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("iarm", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("ggdist", quietly = TRUE)) {
  set.seed(42)
  sim_data <- as.data.frame(
    matrix(sample(0:1, 200 * 10, replace = TRUE), nrow = 200, ncol = 10)
  )
  colnames(sim_data) <- paste0("Item", 1:10)

  # Run 100 iterations sequentially for a quick demo
  cutoff_res <- RMitemInfitCutoff(sim_data, iterations = 100,
                                  parallel = FALSE, seed = 42)
  cutoff_res$item_cutoffs

  # Use the simulations in RMitemInfit()
  RMitemInfit(sim_data, cutoff = cutoff_res)
}
#> Bootstrap p-values are based on 100 iterations, below the recommended 400.
